title: Potassium on Two Clocks
endLine: Potassium moves into cells in minutes; the kidney excretes it over hours.

scenes.tts: We saw water spread into every compartment, so plasma sodium concentration reports water. Potassium breaks that pattern. Almost all of it sits inside cells. So what guards the little that is left outside?
scenes.narration: We saw water spread into every compartment, so plasma sodium concentration reports water. Potassium breaks that pattern. Almost all of it sits inside cells. So what guards the little that is left outside?
scenes.caption: We saw water spread into every compartment, so plasma sodium concentration reports water. Potassium breaks that pattern. Almost all of it sits inside cells. So what guards the little that is left outside?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset (16:9): the wide TANK of pale BLUE shimmering water fills the LEFT 70% of the frame and about 70% of its height, split by a dashed WHITE membrane into 'cells' (left two thirds) and 'outside cells' (right third); the TAP above; the COLLECTING DUCT outlet at bottom right; the tall WHITE gauge at right. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: water pale BLUE; sodium GOLD dots; potassium PURPLE dots; gauge and readings WHITE; sodium-loop hormones ORANGE. New in this film: the sodium-potassium pump RED; insulin TEAL; epinephrine MAGENTA. A small 'schematic' tag sits at bottom left all film. Recap during the first sentence: the gauge reads 'plasma sodium 140'; a ghost pale blue litre pours from the tap and spreads through BOTH parts of the tank, with a faint tag 'last time'; the ghost and tag fade. On 'potassium', the gold dots dim to faint background and the PURPLE dots brighten: the cells part is crowded with them, the outside part holds only about 5 (schematic density). On 'inside cells', the cells part glows. On the question, the gauge relabels 'plasma potassium' and its scale morphs to 3 to 6 (mEq per L), needle at 4.2; white text across the top: 'What guards the potassium outside?'

Title 'Potassium on Two Clocks' fades in over the top band for 2 s while the question text fades out. Purple dots drift in both parts; water shimmers; the needle rests at 4.2. A WHITE outlined band on the gauge from 3.5 to 5 appears, labelled 'usual range'.

scenes.tts: About ninety-eight percent of the body's potassium is inside cells, mostly skeletal muscle. Outside, fourteen litres hold about four point two milliequivalents per litre. That is about fifty-nine, roughly one point seven percent of the body's three thousand five hundred.
scenes.narration: About 98 percent of the body's potassium is inside cells, mostly skeletal muscle. Outside, 14 litres hold about 4.2 mEq per litre. That is about 59, roughly 1.7 percent of the body's 3,500.
scenes.caption: About 98 percent of the body's potassium is inside cells, mostly skeletal muscle. Outside, 14 litres hold about 4.2 mEq per litre. That is about 59, roughly 1.7 percent of the body's 3,500.
scenes.visual: On 'ninety-eight percent', a WHITE label '98% inside' appears over the crowded cells part, and the cells part takes on faint long muscle-fibre stripes, relabelled 'cells, mostly muscle'. On 'fourteen litres', the readout under the outside part reads '14 L' and the needle glows at 4.2. On 'about fifty-nine', a WHITE sum builds under the outside part, size 30: '14 L x 4.2 = about 59 mEq'. On 'one point seven percent', a thin horizontal bar appears along the top of the tank, its full length labelled 'about 3,500 mEq', with a tiny PURPLE sliver at its right end, 1.7% of the bar's length, labelled 'outside: 1.7%'.

scenes.tts: A day's intake is about seventy milliequivalents, more than the whole pool outside the cells. So the first defence is the muscle cell, not the kidney.
scenes.narration: A day's intake is about 70 mEq, more than the whole pool outside the cells. So the first defence is the muscle cell, not the kidney.
scenes.caption: A day's intake is about 70 mEq, more than the whole pool outside the cells. So the first defence is the muscle cell, not the kidney.
scenes.visual: The 3,500 bar and the sum fade. Beside the outside part, two horizontal PURPLE bars appear, drawn to scale: 'outside pool: about 59' and, longer, 'daily intake: about 70' (lengths in the ratio 59 to 70). The TAP, relabelled 'food', fills with purple dots that wait at its mouth. Do NOT show the gauge responding to the intake. On 'the muscle cell', the dashed membrane between the parts glows, and three RED pump icons appear along it, labelled once 'sodium-potassium pump'. On 'not the kidney', the duct outlet at bottom right dims slightly.

scenes.tts: Insulin and epinephrine drive potassium into muscle by stimulating the sodium potassium pump. Insulin acts through its receptor. Epinephrine acts through beta two adrenergic receptors. This shift works in minutes.
scenes.narration: Insulin and epinephrine drive potassium into muscle by stimulating the sodium-potassium pump. Insulin acts through its receptor. Epinephrine acts through beta2-adrenergic receptors. This shift works in minutes.
scenes.caption: Insulin and epinephrine drive potassium into muscle by stimulating the sodium-potassium pump. Insulin acts through its receptor. Epinephrine acts through beta2-adrenergic receptors. This shift works in minutes.
scenes.visual: The two bars fade. The food tap pours its purple dots into the outside part. On 'insulin', TEAL tokens labelled 'insulin' dock on a small TEAL tag 'insulin receptor' beside a pump; on 'epinephrine', MAGENTA tokens labelled 'epinephrine' dock on a small MAGENTA tag 'beta2' beside a pump. The pumps turn faster, and purple dots stream from the outside part through them into the muscle cells part. The needle stays inside the 3.5 to 5 band throughout (schematic). On 'in minutes', a small WHITE clock icon by the pumps sweeps quickly, labelled 'minutes'.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Potassium is defended first by shifting into cells, in minutes. Then the kidney secretes it, over hours.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Potassium is defended first by shifting into cells, in minutes. Then the kidney secretes it, over hours.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Potassium is defended first by shifting into cells, in minutes. Then the kidney secretes it, over hours.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. On 'shifting into cells', the pumps and the 'minutes' clock pulse together and a PURPLE arrow from outside into the cells glows, labelled 'first: into cells'. On 'the kidney', the duct outlet at bottom right brightens again and a second WHITE clock appears beside it, sweeping slowly, labelled 'hours'; a PURPLE arrow from the outside part down into the duct glows, labelled 'then: into urine'. Purple dots keep moving slowly along both arrows.

scenes.tts: The kidney's arm is secretion, not filtration. Glomeruli filter about seven hundred fifty-six milliequivalents a day. The proximal tubule and loop take most of it back. Less than ten percent reaches the distal nephron, a fraction that changes little with diet.
scenes.narration: The kidney's arm is secretion, not filtration. Glomeruli filter about 756 mEq a day. The proximal tubule and loop take most of it back. Less than 10 percent reaches the distal nephron, a fraction that changes little with diet.
scenes.caption: The kidney's arm is secretion, not filtration. Glomeruli filter about 756 mEq a day. The proximal tubule and loop take most of it back. Less than 10 percent reaches the distal nephron, a fraction that changes little with diet.
scenes.visual: The tank slides up and shrinks to the top 45% of the frame (still recognisable, pumps and gauge kept; the food tap fades out for now). The duct outlet unrolls into a horizontal NEPHRON STRIP across the bottom 45% of the frame, flowing left to right, pale BLUE fluid carrying PURPLE dots: at left a round tuft labelled 'filter', then a long tube labelled 'proximal + loop', then a short segment labelled 'distal', ending in the urine outlet. On 'seven hundred fifty-six', a dense stream of purple dots enters at the filter, label 'filtered: about 756 a day'. On 'take most of it back', a broad PURPLE arrow carries most dots from the long tube back up into the tank. On 'less than ten percent', only a thin trickle of purple dots enters the distal segment, label 'under 10%: under 76'.

scenes.tts: Yet urinary potassium follows intake. So the part that rises with intake is secreted. Principal cells release potassium into the tubule through R O M K channels. At high flow, B K channels add more, much of that in intercalated cells.
scenes.narration: Yet urinary potassium follows intake. So the part that rises with intake is secreted. Principal cells release potassium into the tubule through ROMK channels. At high flow, BK channels add more, much of that in intercalated cells.
scenes.caption: Yet urinary potassium follows intake. So the part that rises with intake is secreted. Principal cells release potassium into the tubule through ROMK channels. At high flow, BK channels add more, much of that in intercalated cells.
scenes.visual: Push in on the distal segment until it fills the bottom half of the frame. Its wall shows two cartoon cells side by side: 'principal cell' and 'intercalated cell'; blood (the tank side) above them, tubular fluid below. On 'follows intake', the food tap reappears briefly above the tank and pours; the urine outlet's purple stream thickens to match. On 'secreted', purple dots move from the blood side INTO the cells and OUT into the tubular fluid. On 'principal cells', a RED pump on the principal cell's blood side brings purple dots in, and a PURPLE door on its tubule side opens, labelled 'ROMK'. On 'at high flow', the tubular fluid speeds up and a second PURPLE door opens on the intercalated cell, labelled 'BK (flow)'; more purple dots pour out.

scenes.tts: Two major influences set the rate: aldosterone-type activity, and the sodium and water delivered to these cells. Higher flow raises secretion.
scenes.narration: Two major influences set the rate: aldosterone-type activity, and the sodium and water delivered to these cells. Higher flow raises secretion.
scenes.caption: Two major influences set the rate: aldosterone-type activity, and the sodium and water delivered to these cells. Higher flow raises secretion.
scenes.visual: On 'aldosterone-type activity', an ORANGE token labelled 'aldosterone' (same orange as the sodium loop in the first film) docks on the principal cell, and its ROMK door opens wider. On 'sodium and water delivered', the pale BLUE tubular fluid carrying GOLD sodium dots arrives at the cells from upstream, label 'delivery'. On 'higher flow', the fluid speeds up and purple dots leave both doors faster. Two small dials appear above the cells, 'aldosterone' and 'delivery', each with a needle (schematic, no numbers).

scenes.tts: Aldosterone runs high in two states: after a volume loss, and when plasma potassium is high. In which does the kidney secrete more potassium?
scenes.narration: Aldosterone runs high in two states: after a volume loss, and when plasma potassium is high. In which does the kidney secrete more potassium?
scenes.caption: Aldosterone runs high in two states: after a volume loss, and when plasma potassium is high. In which does the kidney secrete more potassium?
scenes.visual: The distal segment splits into two identical lanes stacked one above the other, each with its principal cell, intercalated cell, ROMK and BK doors. Top lane labelled 'after volume loss'; bottom lane labelled 'high plasma potassium'. An ORANGE 'aldosterone: high' token docks on each principal cell. The tank shrinks to a small icon at top left. Question card across the top in white: 'Which lane secretes more potassium?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: both lanes' fluid flows at the same slow pace, the two orange tokens glow faintly, purple dots bob at the doors without passing.

scenes.tts: When potassium is high. Delivery of sodium and water is normal or higher. Angiotensin two has not risen, and potassium itself stimulates secretion. After a volume loss, delivery is low and angiotensin two is high, which restrains secretion.
scenes.narration: When potassium is high. Delivery of sodium and water is normal or higher. Angiotensin II has not risen, and potassium itself stimulates secretion. After a volume loss, delivery is low and angiotensin II is high, which restrains secretion.
scenes.caption: When potassium is high. Delivery of sodium and water is normal or higher. Angiotensin II has not risen, and potassium itself stimulates secretion. After a volume loss, delivery is low and angiotensin II is high, which restrains secretion.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. BOTTOM lane first: its pale blue fluid with gold sodium dots runs full and fast, label 'delivery: normal or higher'; a faint ORANGE outline 'angiotensin II: not raised'; extra purple dots arrive from the blood side and pour out through ROMK and BK, label 'potassium excreted'. Then TOP lane: its fluid thins to a slow trickle, label 'delivery: low'; a solid ORANGE token 'angiotensin II: high' presses on the ROMK door, which narrows; only a few purple dots pass, label 'potassium kept'.

scenes.tts: Aldosterone is high in both. What differs is what comes with it. One hormone, two outcomes: this is the aldosterone paradox.
scenes.narration: Aldosterone is high in both. What differs is what comes with it. One hormone, two outcomes: this is the aldosterone paradox.
scenes.caption: Aldosterone is high in both. What differs is what comes with it. One hormone, two outcomes: this is the aldosterone paradox.
scenes.visual: On 'high in both', the two ORANGE 'aldosterone: high' tokens pulse together. On 'what comes with it', the delivery labels and the angiotensin II tokens in each lane pulse in turn while the lanes keep flowing (top trickle, bottom full). On 'aldosterone paradox', a WHITE bracket joins the two lanes, labelled 'aldosterone paradox'.

scenes.tts: So potassium has two lines of defence on two clocks. Within minutes, muscle takes up the load. Over hours, the kidney secretes it, steered by aldosterone and by sodium and water delivery.
scenes.narration: So potassium has two lines of defence on two clocks. Within minutes, muscle takes up the load. Over hours, the kidney secretes it, steered by aldosterone and by sodium and water delivery.
scenes.caption: So potassium has two lines of defence on two clocks. Within minutes, muscle takes up the load. Over hours, the kidney secretes it, steered by aldosterone and by sodium and water delivery.
scenes.visual: The two lanes merge back into one distal segment and the camera pulls back to the full world: tank on top with its RED pumps and the 'minutes' clock, nephron strip below with the 'hours' clock, gauge at right. On 'within minutes', the food tap pours, the pumps spin and purple dots stream into the muscle cells part; the 'minutes' clock sweeps fast. On 'over hours', purple dots from the outside part move slowly down through the distal cells and out with the urine; the 'hours' clock sweeps slowly. The needle stays inside the 3.5 to 5 band throughout (schematic).

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (purple dots drifting into the cells and out with the urine, water shimmering). Large white text, centred: 'Potassium moves into cells in minutes; the kidney excretes it over hours.'
